newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN SAYS SEES 97 REAL GDP UP SIX PCT.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN SAYS SEES 97 REAL GDP UP SIX PCT.

text.p: Slovak Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said on Wednesday he expected the country's real GDP to grow by around six percent year-on-year in 1997.
"I think that the Slovak economy will be able to meet the planned target for GDP growth of around six percent, as stated in this year's budget," Kozlik told a news conference.
In 1996, GDP grew by 6.9 percent year-on-year, after 6.8 growth percent in 1995.

National Bank of Slovakia governor Vladimir Masar said earlier this month the bank's monetary programme favoured a slowdown in GDP growth to around five percent year-on-year in 1997 to help decrease the current account deficit to about five percent of GDP, half the 1996 level.
Kozlik's GDP growth estimate was above that of Nomura International, which last November forecast GDP growth would slow to five percent in 1997.
